findings.rationale: The example presents a digon with inverse-oriented edge pairing, then cuts it into two bigons and identifies their boundaries to obtain the sphere. A small polygon/edge-pairing drawing and the two-hemisphere quotient picture would make the quotient relation and cell counts legible at a glance.
findings.concrete_maps_or_relations: Draw the digon sides s1:a and s2:a^{-1} with reversed parameter pairing s1(t)~s2(1-t); show the cut along diameter gamma into B1,B2 and boundary homeomorphism h; optionally pair with Phi([x])=(alpha1(x),+sqrt(1-||alpha1(x)||^2)) on B1 and (alpha2(x),-sqrt(...)) on B2.

findings.rationale: The square schema and its quotient are the central object of this example. A standard square with paired opposite sides would clarify the boundary word, vertex identification and V=1,E=2,F=1 counts.
findings.concrete_maps_or_relations: Draw Q=[0,1]^2 with (s,0)~(s,1) labelled a/a^{-1} and (0,t)~(1,t) labelled b/b^{-1}; all four corners map to one vertex. The quotient map is f(s,t)=(p(s),p(t)) into T^2=(R/Z)^2, constant on exactly these edge-pairing classes.

findings.rationale: This definition is the topological cut-and-glue construction itself. A schematic pair of punctured surfaces with boundary circles identified would clarify the disjoint union and quotient model for readers.
findings.concrete_maps_or_relations: Show S∖int(D_S) and T∖int(D_T), then identify each x on partial D_S with phi(x) on partial D_T; for oriented inputs, indicate phi reverses the induced boundary orientations.

findings.rationale: The statement defines a map of two based coverings over the same base and its essential condition is that it commute with the projections. The conventional commutative square makes the map direction, base map and basepoint condition immediately visible.
findings.concrete_maps_or_relations: Commutative square E1 --f--> E2 with p1 downward to B and p2 downward to B, bottom map id_B; mark f(e1)=e2 and condition (p1)_* pi1(E1,e1) subset (p2)_* pi1(E2,e2).

clean_review: All other assigned items had no confirmed LaTeX/TikZ rendering defects or clearly high-likelihood missing-diagram candidates. Existing mathematical formulas and diagrams were visually checked; proofs were not certified as part of this rendering audit.
